routes.title: Chemical safety: HHPS, WHMIS and safety data

videos.written: Written explanationRead the product label and SDS before use. Match PPE and handling steps to the actual hazard, keep containers controlled, avoid cross-contamination, and know the spill and first-aid response before starting.

Written explanationReaction types describe recurring patterns. Combination joins simpler reactants into a more complex product. Decomposition splits one reactant into simpler products. Combustion involves rapid reaction with oxygen. Replacement reactions rearrange which substances are paired.

Written explanationGas production, a colour change, a temperature change or a new solid can be evidence that substances have reacted. The observation must be interpreted in context: bubbles from boiling and colour from simple mixing do not by themselves prove a chemical reaction. Different starting substances can produce different observations.

Written explanationBreaking bonds requires energy and forming bonds releases energy. A reaction is exothermic when it releases energy overall to its surroundings; it is endothermic when it takes energy in overall. An initial energy input does not determine the net classification.

native.caption: ExothermicProducts have lower chemical energy; net energy leaves the reacting system.EndothermicProducts have higher chemical energy; net energy enters the reacting system.Chemical energy is lower after an exothermic reaction and higher after an endothermic reaction. The arrows represent net transfer, not a particular molecular equation.Original course diagram authored for Science 24.

ReactantsMagnesium and oxygen are the starting substances.ArrowRead the arrow as “produces.”ProductMagnesium oxide is the substance formed.Magnesium and oxygen are reactants; magnesium oxide is the product. The word equation names substances without specifying particle ratios.Original course diagram authored for Science 24.

routes.title: Chemical formulas, common names and states

videos.written: Written explanationA chemical formula identifies the elements and their ratios in a substance. A subscript belongs to the formula and changes substance composition. A coefficient in front of the formula changes only how many particles or formula units are counted.

routes.title: Conservation of mass and balancing equations

videos.written: Written explanationBalancing is an accounting problem. Count each element in the reactants and products, change coefficients to make the counts equal, and recount after every change. Never change a subscript to force a balance because that changes the substance itself.

Written explanationComplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels transfers carbon into carbon dioxide. Adding CO₂ increases the atmosphere’s ability to absorb and re-emit infrared radiation. Energy still leaves Earth, but the balance changes until the climate system reaches a new energy balance.

Written explanationpH is a scale used to describe acidity and basicity. Indicators provide evidence by changing colour. Neutralization involves an acid and a base reacting so that their acidic/basic properties are reduced as new products form.

Written explanationIron rusts when iron, oxygen and water can interact. Paint and other barrier coatings reduce contact with oxygen and water. Galvanizing adds zinc, which can act as both a barrier and a sacrificial metal. A sacrificial metal corrodes preferentially and protects the iron or steel.
